decisions.id: W81-a revert and re-tier E2 -> E3
decisions.summary: the run-on (each thread continued past its end along its own last heading) is reverted because the 48-seed cohort traded seed 03 (newly passing) for seed 42 (newly refused); both partition.py rows stay open (scope kept) at E3, their work the layout that broke
decisions.why: Re-measured this round in a detached worktree with audit/reverted/wave81-run-on.patch applied, against the clone (engine = HEAD): seed 42 passes at HEAD and is REFUSED with the patch (WebRefused: lane 2 breaks the lane law, needle_loops at [2730, 2316]); seed 03 the reverse (refused at HEAD, off_ford). XIII names this exact case: a cohort seed that passed and now fails is a regression, and neither 'the change fixes more than it breaks' nor 'the residue rotated' excuses it, so the 48/54 net does not. The spec's Edge Case 'a fix that changes many maps' gives the route: where making the failing map pass takes more than the row's tier, the row takes that work's tier and its claim stays as found. The failure is in the lane web, outside partition.py, so the fix is a change across modules: E3 by FR-003, as wave 74 was ruled. Ranking by measured work is the request's own principle ('rank all of the findings by how mych implementation work we expect'); the rows are re-ordered, not deferred or dropped, so 'fix all of it' still reaches them in E3 order. The Edge Case's 'waits on a found row' is met by the rows' own fix text, as for waves 69 and 74. Note for when the rows are retaken: XIII's FIX remains the expected exit then - the needle loop on seed 42 is the work, not a reason to leave the rows unfixed.
